Wrap long legend entries based on the plot dimensions

wrapLegend.Rd

Convenience wrapper around wrapLegendLabels() and legendWidthFromPlotDimensions(): derives the maximum number of characters per line from the exported plot dimensions and applies the wrapping to the plot legend in one call.

Usage

wrapLegend(plotObject, plotWidth = NULL, unit = NULL, dpi = NULL, ...)

Arguments

plotObject

A ggplot object, e.g. created by plotTimeProfile(), or a CombinedPlot object whose main plot is updated.

plotWidth

Width of the exported plot. If NULL, the default export width option exportWidth is used.

unit

Unit of plotWidth: one of "cm", "in", "mm" or "px". If NULL, the default export width option exportUnits is used.

dpi

Resolution in dots per inch; used to convert plotWidth to physical inches when unit = "px". If NULL, the default export DPI option exportDpi is used.

...

Additional arguments passed on to legendWidthFromPlotDimensions() (legendFractionHorizontal, legendFractionVertical).

Value

The ggplot object with wrapped legend labels (the input object is not modified).

See also

Other legend helpers: legendWidthFromPlotDimensions(), wrapLegendLabels()

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  time = rep(seq(1, 24), 2),
  concentration = c(dexp(1:24, 0.2), dexp(1:24, 0.1)),
  output = rep(c(
    "Organism|PeripheralVenousBlood|Aciclovir|Plasma (Peripheral Venous Blood)",
    "Organism|PeripheralVenousBlood|Aciclovir|Muscle (Muscle Interstitial)"
  ), each = 24)
)
p <- plotTimeProfile(
  data = df,
  mapping = aes(x = time, y = concentration, color = output)
)
# wrap legend entries to fit a bottom legend on an 8 cm wide plot
pWrapped <- wrapLegend(
  p + theme(legend.position = "bottom"),
  plotWidth = 8,
  unit = "cm"
)
